Nickel foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of nickel foam (1 cm × 1 cm) was sonicated in acetone and water for 6 hours, respectively, and dried under a gentle stream of nitrogen.
nodes.source_text: A piece of nickel foam (1 cm×1 cm) was sonicated in acetone and water for 6 hours, respectively, and dried under a gentle stream of nitrogen.

nodes.name: Immobilization of PFS-b-P2VP micelle seeds on nickel foam
nodes.procedure: The [cleaned] nickel foam was subjected to O₂ plasma treatment for 30 s, and then immersed in a solution of the PFS₄₄-b-P2VP₅₂₆ micelle seeds (150 μl, 0.5 mg ml⁻¹ in isopropanol) for 30 min, and dried under a gentle stream of nitrogen. The resulting nickel foam was aged at room temperature for 1 day and rinsed with isopropanol several times to remove the poorly immobilized micelle seeds and lastly dried under nitrogen flow.
nodes.source_text: The nickel foam was subjected to O₂ plasma treatment for 30 s, and then immersed in a solution of the PFS₄₄-b-P2VP₅₂₆ micelle seeds (150 μl, 0.5 mg ml⁻¹ in isopropanol) for 30 min... aged at room temperature for 1 day

nodes.name: Growth of PFS-b-P2VP micellar brush
nodes.procedure: The PFS₄₄-b-P2VP₅₂₆ micelle seed-coated nickel foam was immersed in 2 ml of isopropanol. Subsequently, 10 μl of a solution of the PFS₂₇-b-P2VP₃₅₆ unimers (10 mg ml⁻¹ in THF) was added. The sample was shaken for 30 min using a shaker and allowed to age for 1 day. Then, the resulting sample was rinsed with isopropanol several times and dried under nitrogen flow.

nodes.name: Pt single atom decoration
nodes.procedure: The PFS-b-P2VP micellar brush-coated nickel foam was immersed in 10 ml of a mixture of 1:1 (v/v) isopropanol/deionized water and then 50 μl of an aqueous solution of Na₂PtCl₄ (10 mg ml⁻¹) was added. After 30 min, the resulting sample was washed with deionized water and isopropanol, and lastly dried under nitrogen flow.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows the Pt SA nanoforest appears erect and uniformly distributed on nickel foam.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Pt-decorated micellar brush appeared to be fairly erect and uniformly distributed on the nickel foam (Fig. 2A and fig. S6).

nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image and corresponding element mapping revealed a homogeneous distribution of N and Pt elements in the micellar brush (Fig. 2B).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-ADF-STEM images show Pt atoms atomically dispersed in the micellar brush with bright spots ~0.17 nm in diameter corresponding to single Pt atoms, without clusters or agglomerates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected annular dark-field STEM (AC-ADF-STEM) images showed that the Pt atoms were atomically dispersed in the micellar brush, without any detectable existence of clusters or agglomerates (Fig. 2C and fig. S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS analysis of Pt SA nanoforest reveals Pt loading of 28.4 wt%, higher than most previously reported Pt SA-based materials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) analysis revealed a large Pt loading of 28.4 wt % (fig. S9), which is higher than most previously reported Pt SA-based materials (table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms high Pt content of 26.59 wt%; Pt 4f shows Pt valence +2 with peak shift to lower binding energy; N 1s shows signal at 398.6 eV (pyridinic N) decreasing with emergence of 399.5 eV signal for N-Pt bond, reaching ca. 66% N-Pt bonding after 30 min immersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive spectrometric (EDS) mapping and x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurements further confirmed the existence of a high content of Pt SA (32.30 and 26.59 wt %, respectively)... High-resolution XPS spectra of N 1s showed that the signal at 398.6 eV (pyridinic N) continuously decreased with the emergence of an additional signal at 399.5 eV... the ratio of N-Pt bonding increased to ca. 66% after immersion for more than 30 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows main peak at ~1.57 Å attributed to N-coordinated Pt SAs; no Pt-Pt scattering path observed compared to Pt foil; fitting suggests each Pt SA coordinates with 3.7 pyridine groups on average.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transformed extended x-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra of the composite showed a main peak at ~1.57 Å... No evidence of Pt-Pt scattering path was observed compared to Pt foil... Fitting of EXAFS spectrum... suggested that each Pt SA coordinated with 3.7 pyridine groups on average.

nodes.characterization_summary: Experimental Pt L₃-edge XANES spectra better match the 4Py-Pt (four pyridine groups) model than 3Py-Pt configuration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Theoretical x-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectrum simulation further showed that the 4Py-Pt... model is in better agreement with the experimental data than the 3Py-Pt configuration (Fig. 2F).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS of Ag SA nanoforest shows major peak at ~1.58 Å ascribed to N-Ag coordination; no Ag-Ag interaction observed compared to Ag foil; fitting reveals each Ag SA coordinates with 2.2 pyridine groups on average.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Taking the Ag SA nanoforest as an example, FT-EXAFS spectra showed a major peak at ~1.58 Å (fig. S30G), which can be ascribed to the N-Ag coordination (40). No Ag-Ag interaction was observed compared to Ag foil... Fitting EXAFS spectrum revealed that each Ag SA coordinated with 2.2 pyridine groups on average (table S4).
